answer: One concrete defense is to price identity at the inlet. Each new agent must lock a refundable stake bonded to unique attested hardware before it can transact, and proven misbehavior slashes that stake. A swarm of 1,000 fakes then needs 1,000 separate locked stakes on 1,000 distinct machines, so an attacker's cost rises linearly instead of being free. Unlike porous karst that hides cheap tunnels under one operator, the attestation is basalt-hard: no concealed path lets a single machine mint many cut-rate identities.
